newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Zairean rebel leader said out of peace talks.
newsitem.headline: Zairean rebel leader said out of peace talks.

text.p: Zairean rebel leader Laurent Kabila has pulled out of an international peace summit intended to bring him into negotiations with President Mobutu Sese Seko, at least for the moment, sources in Angola said on Friday.

An official source in Luanda told Reuters that South African Deputy President Thabo Mbeki "has gone back to the boat to explain that Kabila is not coming tonight. Kabila is not happy with the arrangements. I can't go into what that is."
"My understanding is that Kabila is leaving or has left already for Lubumbashi. We'll try to reconstruct this whole thing later, but obviously it's going to be very difficult," he said.

Mbeki's jet left Luanda Airport at 18.05 p.m. (1705 GMT) for Pointe Noire in Congo where he was expected to join up with international envoys trying to broker peace talks between Zaire's warring sides on board a South African naval ship, the SAS Outeniqua.

Diplomatic sources told Reuters that South African President Nelson Mandela was becoming frustrated by the delays leading up to the planned face-to-face peace talks between Mobutu and Kabila. The sources reported Mandela as saying: "We need to stop wasting time."
